title: High-Impact Teaching Math Tools Without the Price Tag
shortDescription: Free math tools. Purposeful teaching. Make student thinking visible without another subscription.
fullDescription: Math instruction shouldn’t require another subscription. Experience free digital math tools paired with research-informed instructional strategies that make student thinking visible. Through presenter-led demonstrations and quick audience challenges, explore Digital Math Tools for number concepts, GraphSplat for data analysis and mathematical reasoning, and Quiz and Flashcard Studio for retrieval practice. See how modeling, argumentation, feedback, and problem-solving work together. Leave with TEKS-connected lessons, reusable activities, and practical ideas you can use without purchasing another tool.
learningObjectives: Identify free browser-based tools that support mathematics instruction.
Experience research-informed instructional strategies and discuss their purpose.
Use manipulatives, graphs, and recall checks to make mathematical thinking visible.
Plan a short classroom activity with a goal, strategy, tool, and evidence of learning.
Locate and adapt TEKS-connected lesson resources.
imageAlt: Illustrative classroom table with a graph, number line, and hands working with math manipulatives
successCriteria: Explain how a bar-chart baseline changes a visual comparison using values and units.
Choose a representation that fits a mathematical question and explain the match.
Outline a short lesson with a learning goal, strategy, tool, and observable evidence of understanding.

title: Beyond the Rollout: Project Management That Works in K–12
shortDescription: Lead district technology initiatives with clear scope, stakeholder buy-in, milestones, communication, and evidence of sustained adoption.
fullDescription: You know the pattern: the equipment is installed, the announcement goes out, and the rollout still doesn’t work the way people need it to. Let’s look at what makes the difference. We’ll work through a shared district case and connect the decisions to device refreshes, cybersecurity rollouts, infrastructure upgrades, and AI implementation. I’ll show you how to set clear scope, bring the right people into the conversation, connect milestones, manage risks, and keep communication useful. We’ll use ADKAR and Kotter to think about resistance and lasting adoption, then choose KPIs that tell us more than whether installation is complete. You’ll have a few short chances to talk through what you’d do next. Leave with a practical framework and reusable templates for your team. No preparation or project required.
format: Presenter-led instruction with brief decision discussions
learningObjectives: Define scope and identify stakeholders, decision authority, milestones, and dependencies in a district technology initiative.
Choose risk responses and communication that build stakeholder buy-in.
Distinguish delivery KPIs from indicators of use and sustained adoption.
Use a worked example to identify a next action and a response to resistance.
successCriteria: Identify a clear outcome, an exclusion, and an accountable milestone owner in the shared case.
Explain a risk response and a stakeholder communication choice.
Describe one delivery KPI and one adoption KPI with an evidence source and review point.
Recommend a next action that addresses a barrier and supports sustained use.

title: Play, Explore, Explain: Cooperative Learning in Action
shortDescription: Play a game, explore with colleagues, and turn shared activity into explanation, feedback, and classroom ideas.
fullDescription: Want students to do more than play a game or complete a digital activity? Let’s try the activities together and look closely at the thinking they invite. We’ll begin with a short learning game, then work in small groups to explore review, problem-solving, creativity, and formative assessment. You’ll try a shared task, explain your choices, listen to a colleague, and consider what you’d adapt for your learners. Leave with practical ideas and reusable activities. Bring a smartphone, tablet, or laptop; one shared device per group works too.
format: Interactive session with small-group exploration and whole-group sharing
learningObjectives: Experience cooperative learning activities that encourage participation, explanation, and reflection.
Explore instructional activities that support retrieval practice, formative assessment, and deeper learning.
Identify and share practical ways to adapt interactive activities for classroom use.
successCriteria: Help your group complete a shared task while every person explains a choice.
Describe evidence of retrieval, peer explanation, or formative assessment in an activity.
Adapt an activity with a learning goal, a participation routine, and a way to check understanding.
imageAlt: Illustrative adult educators playing and explaining a shared tabletop learning activity
technology: Smartphone, tablet, or laptop; one shared device per small group is enough.
